steps.text: The omnichannel reports show how your team's calls, texts and follow-ups are going, from first lead to closed deal. This video shows which report answers which question, and how the Report Builder reads the same data.

chapters.title: Why these reports
chapters.subtitle: Numbers instead of a to-do list

steps.text: Every call, text and follow-up is an activity. A personal list cannot show how much work is open, who is behind, or which campaign works.
The omnichannel reports answer those questions from your activities, campaigns, dispositions, leads and opportunities. These slides only introduce the ideas; every report is shown on the real pages.
Open Reports in the admin menu. The omnichannel reports sit in several categories, most of them under CRM and Campaigns.
Open Activity summary. The activity reports share the filters Date range, Campaign group, Campaign, Channel, Source, Status and Disposition. Show runs the report, and Export saves it.
Each report needs the View Omnichannel reports permission, set per role under Access Control, Roles. Administrators and Supervisors have it by default.

chapters.title: Volume and completion
chapters.subtitle: How much work there is and how it ends

steps.text: Activity summary is the daily view: total, completed with its rate, pending, in progress, failed and cancelled. Bars split them by source, channel and status.
Campaign performance has one row per campaign, and a second table per campaign group.
Disposition breakdown counts completed activities by the disposition chosen, and its share of all completions.

chapters.title: Backlog and age
chapters.subtitle: What is still open and how late it is

steps.text: Activity backlog looks at all work still open. Unassigned has no owner, Overdue is past its scheduled time, and Reserved is held for an agent right now.
Activity aging puts the same work into age bands, from under an hour to over seven days. A heavy last band is old work nobody touches.
Overdue workload by user shows who holds the late work, how much is unassigned, and its average and maximum age.

chapters.title: Workload by group
chapters.subtitle: The same table, grouped different ways

steps.text: Several reports share one table and change the grouping. Activity source performance groups by origin: manual, automatic by AI, callback, or a dialer mode, with the outcomes, completion rate and average attempts.
CRM channel performance groups by Phone or SMS, Activity kind performance by call or text, and Contact type workload by Lead or Contact.
Activity assignment performance groups by assignment status, and Activity urgency performance by urgency, to check that urgent work finishes first.
Activity attempt analysis shows how many attempts each activity needed and how many completed. Scheduled completion performance compares work finished on schedule with late work.

chapters.title: People
chapters.subtitle: Who does the work and how long it takes

steps.text: Assigned user performance gives each person's activities, outcomes and completion rate. Work nobody owns appears as Not set.
User completion time shows the average, median and maximum time finished work took. Daily user productivity gives the same for each person and day.
Activity creation by user shows who or what created the work, for audits. Not set is work with no recorded creator.

chapters.title: Campaigns, customers and addresses
chapters.subtitle: Mixes, workload per customer and per number

steps.text: Four campaign reports break each campaign down by source, channel, disposition and number of attempts, with the completion rate of each row.
Customer workload has one row per customer, to spot someone contacted too often.
Address usage compares your sales line, support line and text line.

chapters.title: Dialer and AI
chapters.subtitle: Every dialed number, and what the AI handled

steps.text: Dialer call detail lists one row per number the dialer worked, with contact, campaign, last disposition, attempts, agent and status. It opens on the Dialer source, a page at a time.
AI handoff and containment counts the conversations an AI profile finished itself and those it passed to a live agent, with the rates, the time to escalate and the reasons.
Lead funnel shows leads created in the period by their current status, and the conversion rate. The three CRM reports use the date range only.
Lead conversion by source and list shows, for each, how many leads converted, the rate and the average time to convert.
Opportunity pipeline lists open deals by stage with amount and weighted amount, using the stage's probability, then the win rate and amount won for deals closed in the period.

chapters.title: In the Report Builder
chapters.subtitle: The same data, your own report

steps.text: The Report Builder reads the same records. Open Reports, Report Builder, New Report, then Add data set.
The Omnichannel source offers Activities, Dispositions, Campaigns, Campaign groups and Activity batches. Contacts, leads and opportunities are under Content items.
Add Activities. The window then lists related data sets, such as the activity's disposition and campaign, which are joined for you.
The Messaging source offers Conversations and Messages, with each outbound text's delivery status but never its text. Add Messages.
Drag Delivery status and Number of rows onto Columns, and the preview counts texts by delivery status.

chapters.title: Use cases
chapters.subtitle: Three ways teams use these reports

steps.text: Morning stand-up: a supervisor opens Activity backlog, then Overdue workload by user, and reassigns late work before anyone dials.
Campaign review: compare Campaign performance, Campaign disposition mix and Lead conversion to decide which campaign to repeat.
AI rollout: watch AI handoff and containment. A falling containment rate, or a common escalation reason, shows where the AI profile needs better instructions.
The omnichannel reports turn activities, campaigns, leads and deals into numbers you can act on. Thanks for watching.
